text.p: Two goals from Juventus super-sub Michele Padovano in Sunday night's 2-0 away win against Lazio served as a timely reminder of the 30-year-old striker's versatility.

Unusually for him, Padovano started Sunday night's game on the pitch and not the sub's bench, stepping in for Croat striker Alen Boksic who last week was ruled out for two months because of an ankle injury.

And his goals not only sent league leaders Juventus four points clear of second-placed Sampdoria at the exact halfway point in the 34-game Italian season but they also prompted fulsome praise from his coach, Marcello Lippi.
"He's a player who can come on, ready to go and capable of scoring important goals with a certain regularity. For me such a player is a class footballer," said Lippi.
Since joining Juventus last season, Padovano's role has normally been that of reserve to such as Boksic this year and to Gianluca Vialli and Fabrizio Ravanelli last season.
But despite limited opportunities, Padovano has regularily made his presence felt scoring four league goals last season while Sunday's double brings his tally for this season to six.
Perhaps more important were the goals he scored along the Juventus road to winning last season's European Champions Cup.

Not only did Padovano score against German side Borussia Dortmund in the first round and against Spanish side Real Madrid in the quarter finals, but he also scored one of the shoot-out penalties which saw Juventus defeat Dutch side Ajax Amsterdam in the final in Rome last May.

Even Padovano's best friends would have to concede that he is a late maturing player since prior to joining Juventus, he had seemed little more than a journeyman professional with sides such as Cosenza, Pisa, Napoli, Genoa and Reggiana.
Goals have always come his way, however, since his Serie A total now stands at 54 in seven and a half seasons.
Lazio coach Zdenek Zeman pointed out on Sunday night just how much Padovano has improved since his early days with Cosenza.
"He's a player who has evolved a great deal since I first knew him in the third division,".
Padovano himself was understandably pleased with his performance on Sunday.
"We moved ahead of our closest rivals such as Sampdoria, Inter and Vicenza and for me it couldn't have gone better, that was my best game for Juventus, and not just for the goals".
Padovano also believes that he can do even better given the prospect of a sustained run in the team because of the injury to Boksic.
"You just have to look at my record over recent seasons, for me it's normal to be always in the team.
"Here at Juventus, we have a special situation and I adapt and do as the coach (Lippi) says but if I'm now to get a continuous run in the team, no problems, on the contrary, it's better for me".
